irregularities.title: Luminosity vs HOTU is a maker-quoted market with $7.25 of lifetime volume
irregularities.detail: The published 52.5/47.5 replays exactly from the Polymarket book, and the book carries $15,977 of liquidity, but the market has traded $7.25 in total (gamma volume, read 2026-10-26T00:52Z). A reader should treat it as one market maker's quote, not as a crowd consensus. The row is left as published; the spread rule that qualifies it (0.03) is about depth, not about traded interest, so the page does not claim a traded price.

irregularities.title: The repo review page still quotes a 98.2% HOTU figure the site no longer publishes
irregularities.detail: data/research/27ac20d6/flags.json ("27ac20d6-1082792-magnitude") states the fixture is "published at HOTU 98.2% / The Huns 1.8% from the project's own bo3.gg network model" and that "the Polymarket book ... is 43 cents wide (rejected by the project's own 0.15 ceiling)". Both sentences describe the 2026-10-25 build. The 2026-10-26T01:04:20Z build publishes HOTU 87.0% from a 0.10-wide book (82-92 cents, verified first-hand at 2026-10-26T00:53Z). The flag's own prediction came true, but a reader on the review page is still told the site publishes 98.2%. Correcting that text is outside this session's file scope (data/research/27ac20d6 is another session's record) and is logged as a change request in COORDINATION.md.

irregularities.title: LFO 10 vs ex-6666 is the widest-uncertainty row on the board and it is labelled as such
irregularities.detail: The row is the project's results-based fit: LFO 10 has 10 anchored series, a posterior SD of 114.7 points and a prior centre of 981, which is scored with the fit rule RD = 150 + 300/sqrt(10) = 244.87 points rather than Valve's 75. Replaying that rule reproduces the published 39.0% / 61.0% exactly, and the row publishes a one-sigma interval of 18.4%-64.5% plus "low_confidence": true. No money line is used: the Polymarket order book for the same fixture is 0.53 wide and is recorded as refused rather than averaged.

irregularities.title: The checked-in data/origination.json is an eleven-day-old replay fallback, not the live board
irregularities.detail: data/origination.json in the worktree is dated 2026-10-15T09:31:24Z with 17 rows; the live board is the root origination.json (2026-10-26T01:04:30Z, 19 rows), which the publisher copies to /data/origination.json on deploy. This is documented behaviour (root_publish replay fallback), not a defect, but anyone reading the repository while auditing the site will see the older file first.
